The third review of 1.24.34's lift station change (0dfc9d8..b46217e, src/lantern.inner.html), 2026-11-23.
Written without reading tests/fixtures/liftstation_review1_1234/, liftstation_review2_1234/ or tests/review*_liftstation_1234.py
(read afterwards only to make the cases differ from theirs: one title was changed).

How it was run
  node tests/fixtures/liftstation_review3_1234/replay.js [lantern.inner.html] [id regex]
  The draft and 1.24.33 (git show 0dfc9d8, written to the temp folder) are loaded side by side in jsdom (load.js, a copy of
  liftstation_review1_1230's); the model is scripted. The duplex control circuits are run by liftstation_review1_1230/sim.js
  (fill and pump-down: which coil runs at which level, the alternation, the lag, the alarm, an overload).
  run_b46217e.txt is the run: 282 cases, 242 AGREE, 40 DISAGREE (cases_a..h.js; a case AGREEs when Lantern does what is
  right for that input, whatever 1.24.33 did).

What held (the guard)
  - 47 right circuits of every kind a model writes (series, parallel through junctions and direct, ladders of 3 and 4 lamps
    as wire chains, meters across parts by double wire, by junctions and by numbered terminals, ammeter in line, LED and
    resistor, motor and switch, a fuse as a resistor, a ground as the return four ways and an implied GND, B1+ / B1-,
    L1.1 / L1.2, "wire A B C", arrows, "to", reversed wires, a wire written twice, lower and mixed case, RC, a capacitor
    across the supply, cells in series, flyback and series diodes, an LED branch across a motor, a changeover, a solar
    panel charging a battery): none questioned by the two new checks (cases_a A-series-2 .. A-vm-ports).
  - The bench: all 300 questions go to the same tools with the same instructions as 1.24.33 (E-bench-300). Every saved
    bench reply with a MAKE block (467 replies of 328 rows in 83 files) builds as in 1.24.33 but two rows, and solved and
    graded every row passes or fails as it did (G-bench-build, G-bench-grade). The two rows that changed are both
    make-parallel-lamps, both failing before and after: bench_run_1244_2b (its last reply: L2 wired to V1 only, now said --
    right, G-1244-2b-parallel-L2) and bench_run_1247_08b (its first reply -- see A-masks-parallel-line below).
  - The open circuit's line: right in 19 of its 23 cases (the end a lamp, a switch after a load, a motor, a capacitor, an LED --
    which, copied, gets Lantern's resistor --, an ammeter after a resistor, a coil, two cells, the 35B's resistor chain,
    a ground end, four loads to one ground, a stop switch named before the line), and withheld where it would short the
    source (an ammeter alone, a switch alone, a switch to the ground beside the lamp, the ground past a switch, two ends).
  - MAKE STATION: the second start float with its own tag is the lag, and said; a redundant start (1.24.33: an off float)
    the lag, said; a third start in a duplex, a second lag in a duplex, a second start in a simplex: not drawn, said;
    a triplex's two lag floats by tag, by height, by "Lag 1"/"Lag 2" in straight quotes, by pump 1/2/3 on and start 1/2/3;
    four pumps' three lags; emergency high as the alarm (1.24.33 dropped it); a high level alarm and an emergency high as
    two alarms; MAKE LEVELS with emergency high and start 1/start 2, MAKE CONTROL with pump 1/2 on and all pumps on, read
    as the station: all drawn and the duplex control runs right (cases_c).
  - floatJob: 38 labels read right, and 12 MAKE CONTROL duplexes with the new labels (pump 1/2 on, start 1/2, start #1/#2,
    P1/P2, all pumps on, emergency shutdown and low water cutoff under the off float, shutdown, emergency high, emergency
    high with a high high, emergency high - start both pumps) simulated: each runs as a duplex should; a redundant start
    beside the lead goes back once with the line that writes it as the lag, and the line copied runs (cases_f). A simplex
    sump's "shutdown" and "high level" floats are now made a hold-in (F-c-simplex-shutdown).
  - Chat: a schematic then MAKE STATION, MAKE STATION then MAKE CONTROL, MAKE STATION twice, a control then a station, a
    table beside a station or beside a circuit sent back, a table rewritten in the correction, two circuits in two blocks:
    each made once, what differs said (cases_d). Adam's own chat: the station, nothing asked again (D-adam-chat).

FINDINGS (high first; "as in 1.24.33" marks a gap the change left, not one it made)

HIGH
1. E-electrical-adam, E-electrical-adam-reply (high); E-electrical-draw, E-electrical-give-two, E-control-panel (medium);
   E-please (low). As in 1.24.33.
   Adam's question with one word added -- "Write the electrical schematic for a typical lift station" -- still goes to
   MAKE SCHEMATIC with the hobby parts (battery, lamp, motor), the exact failure this change was made for. views() reads
   "electrical" (or "control panel") as the control drawing alone; asks() takes a station only with no view named or two,
   so it returns false; AI_CONTROL's asks() does not take "electrical schematic for a lift station" either. And because
   asks() is false, the 35B's own reply of Adam's chat under this question is not read as the station: it is sent back
   with "there is no electrical part called breaker ... transformer ...". The same for "Draw the electrical schematic for
   a lift station", "Give me the electrical schematic for a lift station with two pumps", "Write the schematic for a lift
   station's control panel", "Lift station schematic please".
   Expected: a station's electrical schematic (one view named, no other machine) goes to MAKE STATION showing the control
   (or to MAKE CONTROL), and a part-and-wire reply to it is read as the station.

MEDIUM
2. A-two-circuits, A-transformer (medium); A-motor-generator (low). New in 1.24.34.
   The "not joined to the circuit of B1" check sends back right circuits whose second part is joined by no wire: two
   example circuits side by side in one block (each with its own battery), a transformer drawn as two inductors (MAKE
   SCHEMATIC has no transformer part), a motor turning a generator ("generator" is a source by SYN). 1.24.33 drew all
   three; now nothing is drawn and the line is "wire them into it, or leave them out". Copied, the first spoils the
   example; for the transformer it wires the lamp's circuit into the 120 V primary -- what a transformer is there to
   prevent.
   Expected: the check only where the parts apart have no source of their own and no coil (inductor) among them; or say
   "draw each circuit in a MAKE SCHEMATIC block of its own" (rest() now makes a reply's second block).
3. C-lag-alarm-one-float (medium); C-lag-alarm-plus-hh (low). Changed in 1.24.34.
   MAKE STATION with one float "lag on / high level alarm" (a small panel's): spec() now makes it the lag, and MAKE CONTROL
   still lights LT3 "high level alarm" on it (its "added" says so) -- but the station's summary says "no high level alarm
   float: the block has none", "What Lantern does not know" says "This station has no high level alarm", and the checks
   never lift FS3 for the alarm. 1.24.33 said the alarm (and not the lag). With a high high alarm above it
   (C-lag-alarm-plus-hh), one light now hangs on both floats (1.24.33: a light each) and the checks lift FS3 only for the
   pumps. Expected: both jobs said and checked, as the control drawn has them.
4. C-two-offs-tagged (medium). Changed in 1.24.34 (1.24.33 sent it back, its line also keeping the lower).
   Two floats both called "off" with tags and heights -- FS5 "off" 1.5 ft written first, FS1 "off" 2 ft -- the first
   written is drawn as the station's one off float and FS1 is "not drawn ... both pumps stop on it": the pumps now pump
   the well 6 in lower than the model's off float, which Lantern's own text says is set by the pumps' minimum submergence.
   Expected: the higher off float is the pumps' off and the lower a redundant one (as Lantern's own off2 sits below off).
5. C-jobless-top-down, C-jobless-top-down-copied, C-jobless-below-off, C-jobless-numbered (medium). The distinct jobs are
   new in 1.24.34; the inch reading is 1.24.33's.
   The jobs handed to floats with no job go out in the order written, not by height. Four floats written top down (5, 4,
   3, 2 ft) are handed "off" 5 ft, "lead on" 4 ft, "lag on" 3 ft, "high level alarm" 2 ft -- copied, Lantern sends the
   block back again (three "is not above" problems), a round the bench does not have. A jobless float at 1 ft under the off
   float at 2 ft is handed "lead on" 1 ft, a start below the stop (1.24.33 the same). And floats named "Float 1".."Float 4"
   in straight quotes: parse()'s inch-mark rule reads 1" as 1 inch, so the lines handed back are float FS1 "off" 1 in ...
   4 in -- heights nobody wrote; copied, the station is drawn with its floats an inch apart (said under the levels).
   Expected: with heights, the jobs by height (bottom up); a float under the off float not a start; no height made of a
   name's number (the inch rule only after the closing quote of a label, not inside it -- fq() does this for Lantern's own
   lines already).
6. C-tri-floats-word-line (medium); C-dup-floats-lead-lead (low). As in 1.24.33.
   A triplex written in the guide's own form, "floats off lead lag lag alarm", is drawn with one lag float and nothing
   said: the third pump's start is dropped without a word (the new rule takes a second lag only with a tag or a height).
   "floats off lead lead alarm" for a duplex: the second start dropped, nothing said.
   Expected: two lags for 3+ pumps (key lag1/lag2 in order), or the drop said.
7. D-levels-then-station (medium). New in 1.24.34.
   A reply of MAKE LEVELS with every height (well 10 ft, floats at 2, 3, 4, 5 ft) then a bare MAKE STATION: the station is
   drawn from MAKE STATION with no heights, and nothing anywhere says the levels block was not read (the wrapper's note
   is added only when differs() finds a pump count, a float job or a horn; it never compares heights). In the other order
   Chat says it "did not read it" (D-station-then-levels agrees). Expected: the heights carried (the levels block is a
   given view), or at least said.
8. E-neg-do-not (medium); E-neg-already, E-neg-without, E-neg-done (low). Changed in 1.24.34 (ALLNOT).
   "Do not include any other drawings; just write the schematic for a lift station": WHOLE_W makes it a station, ALLNOT keeps
   allDrawn() false -- and a station question naming no view draws all three anyway. The negation has no effect anyone can
   see. Expected: the schematic alone (the control), when the question says no other drawings.
9. E-electrical-drawings-picture (medium). As in 1.24.33.
   "Write up the electrical drawings for the Main Street lift station" goes to MAKE DRAWING, the picture of shapes on a
   20 x 12 grid ("electrical" is one view, so not the station; "drawings" is the picture's word).

LOW
10. A-one-side-not-drawn, A-masks-parallel-line (low). New in 1.24.34.
   The two new checks are in parseSchematic, so a circuit they question is not drawn at all (1.24.33 drew a closed lamp
   circuit with a voltmeter on one lead; the hooks' own questions are drawn and sent back, 1.13.4), and they run before
   the draw hooks: in bench_run_1247_08b's make-parallel-lamps reply (a second source V2 on one wire AND the lamps wired to
   each other) the model is now told only about V2; 1.24.33 told it the lamps were in series, with the four lines that
   make them parallel. One correction, so the line that answers the question is lost. Expected: both said, or the one-side
   and apart checks as late (drawn) problems after the hooks'.
11. B-ladder-no-return (low). The parallel ladder with its return missing (B1-J1, J1-L1, J1-L2, L1-J2, L2-J2): every way
   ends at J2, and "wire J2 B1" is withheld because J2 has two wires, not one. The bench's parallel lamps slip.
12. B-vm-in-series, B-fuse-alone (low). The line counts a voltmeter and any resistor as a load: B1-VM1-L1 is handed
   "wire L1 B1", which closes a loop the next check sends back (a voltmeter in series); a fuse written as a resistor alone
   on the battery is handed "wire F1 B1", a fuse straight across the battery.
13. B-two-ground-symbols (low; as in 1.24.33). The battery's minus to G1 and the lamp to G2 -- every schematic's common
   ground -- is "not closed". A guard case of "a ground used as return".
14. C-second-lead-lower (low). Two "lead on" floats, the second written lower (3 ft under 3.5 ft): the second written is made
   the lag whatever its height, then the block goes back for its lag (labelled "lead on (lag on)", words the model never
   wrote) being under the lead. Expected: the lower start is the lead.
15. C-pump2-off (low). "pump 2 on" is the lag's start, but "pump 2 off" is "not drawn ... both pumps stop on it", where
   "lag off" would be drawn as the lag pump's own off float. Said, so low.
16. D-ctl-pip-station-note (low). MAKE CONTROL, MAKE PIPING, MAKE STATION: Chat's note says "Lantern made the station from
   the block before it" -- made.block is the control block, whose action is not whole -- when it was made from the MAKE
   STATION block after both.
17. D-held-self-fix-twice (low). A reply whose first block is broken and whose second is the AI's own fix, then the
   correction: the held fix and the corrected block are both shown -- the same circuit twice (only a byte-identical
   correction is dropped). The 0.8B's make-music-ode reply in bench_run_1.24.31_0.8b is this shape (two MUSIC blocks, the
   first failing).
18. E-pid-no-tool, E-draw-them (low). "Please produce a P&ID for a sewage lift station" goes to no tool: DRAWOBJ names
   P&IDs but SHOWV does not, and asks() returns before WHOLE_W. "What are the drawings needed for a lift station? Draw
   them." goes to MAKE DRAWING: AI_PARTS splits it and "Draw them" alone is the picture's (allDrawn()'s own example, said
   another way; "What drawings does a lift station need? Draw them" works).
19. F-fallback-agrees (low). AI_PUMP_STATION's fallback floatJob (AI_CONTROL dropped) reads start 2, start #2, start 3,
   pump 3 on, pump two/three on, P2 on, P3 start, start pump 2 as lead (AI_CONTROL: lag), and assist, Hi Level, Lo Level,
   Hi-Hi, top float, bottom float as nothing. The comment "AI_PUMP_STATION's fallback says the same" holds for the
   emergency words only. F-pump-no-2 (low, as in 1.24.33): "Pump No. 2 On" is the lead.
20. H-title-power-street, H-title-control-road (low). A station read from part-and-wire blocks whose name has a view's word
   in it -- "Power Street Lift Station Electrical", "Control Road Lift Station" -- is titled "Pump station": the rule cuts
   from "power"/"control" to the end.

What was not run
  - No model: every reply is scripted (the saved bench replies, Adam's chat, and replies written here). Nothing was run on
    the 35B, the 4B, the 2B or the 0.8B, and the GitHub bench was not started (no push).
  - No browser: the drawings were not rendered or looked at (jsdom has no canvas); Chat's notes were read as text from
    rec.notes, not as shown.
  - The PIPING view and the parts list were checked only where a case names them.
